subject: SIG: Subprocessor roster + telemetry/data-routing details
messages:
From: Jordan Simon <jordan.simon@acme-corp.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acme-corp.com, security@acme-corp.com
Date: Tue, 8 Dec 2026 16:22:00 -0800
Subject: SIG follow-up: subprocessor list + telemetry routing questions

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. As part of our vendor due diligence for production acceptance, our security team is looking for a complete subprocessor roster and clarifications on how telemetry and support tooling data flows are routed and retained. Specifically:

- A single-sheet list of subprocessors (cloud infra, monitoring/observability, support/ticketing, error-tracking) with purpose and data types in scope.
- Whether telemetry (metrics/traces/logs) ever contains PII or customer content; if so, how it is redacted or pseudonymized.
- Which providers store logs/evidence for >90 days and where (region).
- Any SOC2/SIG evidence we can reference (report, Syslogs, attestation).

Can you send the roster and any pointers to evidence by EOD next Monday? Our procurement team will also need a copy for the contract binder.

Appreciate the quick turnaround,

Jordan
Jordan Simon
Security Program Manager, Acme Payments
security@acme-corp.com

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Jordan Simon <jordan.simon@acme-corp.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 09:14:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: subprocessor list + telemetry routing questions

Jordan —

Thanks for the note. Attached is an exported roster (spreadsheet) that lists our subprocessors by category, purpose, data types processed, and retention windows. High-level answers inline below; details are in the attached sheet and the network diagram link.

- Cloud infra: Primary compute/storage in AWS (us-west-2) + GCP for backups (us-east1). See sheet tab "cloud_infra".
- Observability: Datadog for metrics/traces, Sentry for error tracking, and an internal ingest pipeline that strips request bodies before indexing.
- Support/ticketing: Zendesk (ticket text is retained per customer config; we routinely redact PII on request).
- Retention: Default telemetry retention is 30 days for full fidelity traces; aggregated metrics retained 13 months. Raw logs sent to long-term archive are encrypted and stored in GCP (us-east1) for up to 3 years only when required for legal/audit reasons.
- PII: We do not store customer prompt content in telemetry by default. Prompt/text capture is opt-in at the customer level and requires a data processing addendum; when enabled we route that data to a customer-scoped project with strict ACLs.

Attachments: Redwood_SIG_Subprocessors_2026-12-10.xlsx, SOC2_Type2_Redwood_2025.pdf, network-dataflow-diagram.png

I've cc'd Vivek (TAM) for any customer-specific retention exceptions and Monica from Security for evidence/context. Rishi is on for any legal redline/contract questions.

Next steps: If you want, we can walk the roster with your security team next week and map each row to the SIG controls.

Best,

Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0181

From: monica_patel@redwood.com
To: Jordan Simon <jordan.simon@acme-corp.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 11:07:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: subprocessor list + telemetry routing questions

Jordan — quick follow-up from Security. A couple of clarifications to expect in the roster:

1) "Data types in scope" column indicates whether the subprocessor sees any of these: Auth tokens (no), customer prompts (only if customer opts-in), logs/metrics (yes but redacted), user identifiers (hashed/pseudonymized).

2) For Datadog/Sentry we have filters at ingest that redact JSON fields tagged in our schema as "sensitive". We can provide the redact rules (annotated list) under NDA or in a controlled evidence folder if Acme needs it for SIG validation.

3) Regarding long-term archives: only exported logs stored beyond 180 days are placed into GCP cold storage after an approval workflow and are encrypted with customer-key options for enterprise customers.

If you send over the SIG template rows you care most about, we can flag/highlight rows that satisfy each control.

-Monica
Monica Patel
Information Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com

From: Jordan Simon <jordan.simon@acme-corp.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acme-corp.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 08:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: subprocessor list + telemetry routing questions

Thanks — this is helpful. A couple quick asks before we move the SIG template to our control owners:

- Can you confirm which subprocessors are used for incident response and whether incident response runbooks contain any customer content by default?
- We need a signed location for the SOC2 report; can you share the signed attestation or a redacted version we can place in our binder?
- Please confirm whether Datadog/Sentry are accessible from EU IPs when data is scoped to EU customers (we flag cross-border telemetry concerns).

If you can get these answers by EOD Wednesday it will keep our procurement checklist on schedule.

Jordan

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Jordan Simon <jordan.simon@acme-corp.com>, procurement@acme-corp.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 09:13:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SIG follow-up: subprocessor list + telemetry routing questions

Jordan — quick answers inline: 

- Incident response: We engage PagerDuty (on-call orchestration) and an external IR contractor (BlueShield Security) for escalations. Incident runbooks do not contain full customer prompt text by default; they contain event ids, metadata, and truncated contextual logs. If a customer has enabled prompt capture for debugging, runbooks may reference the event id for retrieval from the customer-scoped archive (access is logged and restricted).

- SOC2 evidence: Attached is a redacted SOC2 Type II report and an attestation letter (we can provide the signed attestation PDF for your binder; see attachment).

- EU telemetry: For EU-scoped customers we configure regional projects and EU-only Datadog instances where possible. Sentry can be configured to an EU-hosted cluster; we will flag rows in the roster to indicate EU-only deployments. Cross-border exports only occur with explicit customer consent or under legal process.

I've updated the attached spreadsheet to add an "EU-scoped?" column and a "used for incident response?" flag. If you want a short walkthrough, Vivek can schedule a 30-min call with your security and procurement teams tomorrow.

Best,

Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
